title: Theo and the Bridge
premise: In 1938, apprentice clockmaker Gideon Reyes is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock, where she discovers a hidden compartment containing documents proving her late mentor once sheltered a fugitive scientist now declared an enemy of the state. When a child is left at her door with instructions to forget the face, Gideon realizes the girl is that scientist's daughter and the papers are both her inheritance and her death warrant. Torn between loyalty to her mentor's memory and the truth that could save or destroy her, she must smuggle the child and the evidence across the border before the master clock's final chime. She succeeds at a terrible cost: burning her own name, her workshop, and everything she cannot carry.
about_author: Noor Voss is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing displaced-persons records from interwar Europe. She writes historical fiction about ordinary people caught in machinery larger than themselves.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Things
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV: summoned to the observatory to repair the master clock, she finds her mentor Herr Anselm's hidden ledger inside its case—names, dates, payments for silence. Beat: curiosity curdling into dread as she realizes the clock was never just a clock.

chapters.title: Instructions in Chalk
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV: a child appears at her workshop door at dawn with a chalked note—forget the face—and no name. Neighbors watch; the constable asks questions. Beat: fear and reluctant tenderness as Gideon hides the girl among clock parts.

chapters.title: What Anselm Owed
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV: reading the ledger fully, she reconstructs how Anselm smuggled Dr. Marek Voss out years ago and took blood money to stay quiet. The child is Voss's daughter. Beat: grief and betrayal—her inheritance is complicity.

chapters.title: The Inspector's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Inspector Brandt, POV: a polite, patient man interviews Gideon about Anselm's affairs. He notices the second teacup. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension; Gideon lies well but not perfectly, and knows it.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Debt
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV: her brother Tomas, a party member, warns her that names are being collected and offers protection—if she surrenders the child. Beat: the loyalty-vs-truth theme sharpened into family fracture; she refuses and loses him.

chapters.title: Eleven Minutes Slow
chapters.summary: Gideon and the girl, alternating POV: they hide in the observatory while Brandt searches the town. The girl reveals her father left a key sewn in her coat matching the ledger's lock. Beat: fragile trust forming under threat.

chapters.title: The Price List
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV: a smuggler agrees to move them across the border—for the ledger itself, which would expose other protectors still alive. Beat: moral crisis; paying with other people's safety to buy one child's survival.

chapters.title: Chime Before Midnight
chapters.summary: Brandt, POV: closing in, he corners Gideon at the observatory and offers the same bargain Tomas did. She triggers the master clock's mechanism, jamming it mid-chime to mask the smugglers' departure. Beat: climax—defiance measured in seconds.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV: at the border crossing, the smuggler demands proof there are no copies. Gideon burns the ledger page by page, keeping only the girl's hand in hers. Beat: sacrifice—the truth survives only as memory now.

chapters.title: A New Escapement
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV, two years later: working under a new name in a foreign city, she teaches the girl to file her first gear wheel. A letter arrives unsigned: 'The clock still runs.' Beat: quiet resolution—inheritance remade as craft, loyalty kept without witness.
